item.research_question: How do different hot forming routes (hot rolling vs. hot extrusion) influence the ductile-to-brittle transition (DBT) behavior, specifically DBTT and upper shelf energy (USE), in two similar Fe-Cr-Al oxide dispersion strengthened (ODS) stainless steels with comparable microstructures?
item.material_system: PM2000 (Fe-Cr-Al ODS, hot rolled tube) and MA956 (Fe-Cr-Al ODS, hot extruded bar)
item.processing_route: Mechanical alloying followed by hot-compaction, hot extrusion, and/or hot rolling at approximately 1050 °C, followed by air cooling to room temperature.
item.test_conditions: Tensile tests: -196 °C to 300 °C, strain rate 5 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; Charpy impact tests: -197 °C to 425 °C, impact energy 300 J, velocity 5.4 ms⁻¹; Specimen orientations: PM2000 (LT, LS), MA956 (LR).
key_findings: The hot forming routes do not significantly influence the microstructure but cause differences in texture and oxide particle distribution.
Tensile properties are little affected by the different forming routes.
The DBT temperature and upper shelf energy (USE) are significantly affected by the delamination orientation relative to the notch plane.
In PM2000 (hot rolled), delaminations are parallel to the rolling surface (L-T plane), whereas in MA956 (hot extruded), they are randomly oriented due to transverse isotropy.
For PM2000 LT-notched specimens, the lower shelf energy (LSE) is 1 J, while for LS-notched specimens, it is significantly higher at 3 J.
MA956 exhibits a higher LSE value (50% higher than PM2000 LT-notch) despite similar grain size and cleavage fracture mechanism, attributed to a higher density of secondary cracks/delaminations.
No upper shelf energy (USE) was observed for PM2000 LS-notched specimens or MA956, with a maximum absorbed energy recorded at approximately 150 °C.
The MA956 alloy is transversely isotropic, leading to random delamination orientation, while PM2000 has a strong {001}<110> texture component.
item.mechanism: The difference in DBT behavior is attributed to the orientation of delaminations relative to the notch plane: in PM2000 LT specimens, delaminations act as 'crack dividers' decreasing DBTT and USE, while in LS specimens they act as 'crack arresters' increasing USE. The transverse isotropy of MA956 leads to random delamination orientation, which positively affects absorbed energy compared to the aligned delaminations in PM2000.
item.limitations: The accuracy of the Charpy test machine scale gradation was 1 J, and the time between specimen removal from the bath and fracturing might vary, preventing positive inference on LSE values for LT-notch positions between alloys.
quotes: The two hot forming routes considered do not significantly influence the microstructure, but cause differences in the texture and the distribution of oxide particles.
Whereas in hot rolled material the delaminations are parallel to the rolling surface, in the hot extruded material, they are randomly oriented because the material is transversally isotropic.

The MA956 alloy is transversely isotropic because axisymmetric forms during the extrusion processing, whereas in the PM2000 alloy, the tangential and radial directions become parallel to the <110> and <100> directions during the rolling processing.
